entries.subject: V-band reflectance
entries.finding: JAXA ONC v06 corrected numeric map. Its 0–0.035 display is distinct from the brightness-matched color composite.

entries.subject: Color composite
entries.finding: [Hirata et al. 2026 ONC mapping release](https://doi.org/10.7910/DVN/WW3IH0). Channels p/v/ul are false color, not natural color.

entries.subject: Shape and Elevation
entries.finding: The retained native DSK label identifies the March 2020 SPC model, about 200,000 plates, from ONC-T/W1/W2 observations spanning 2018-06-19 to 2019-11-19. Its 2025 publication/transport creation is distinct from the model version. The label’s 1950–2050 time bounds are SPICE coverage, not decades of observations. The selected model supports map registration and source radius relative to 448 m; it is not a new 2025 surface reconstruction.

entries.subject: Equatorial close-up
entries.finding: [JAXA JADE2 ONC I/F mosaic](https://jlpeda.jaxa.jp/en/product/archive/detail_02/), acquired during MASCOT deployment on 3–4 October 2018. It is a spacecraft photograph mosaic, not a lander photograph.

entries.subject: Thermal inertia
entries.finding: [JAXA JADE2 numeric map](https://jlpeda.jaxa.jp/en/product/archive/detail_02/), based on [Shimaki et al. (2020)](https://doi.org/10.1016/j.icarus.2020.113835). Model-derived resistance to heating and cooling, in J m⁻² K⁻¹ s⁻½.

entries.subject: Spectral slope
entries.finding: [JAXA JADE2 b–x map](https://jlpeda.jaxa.jp/en/product/archive/detail_02/), from ONC normal albedo and the distribution reported by [Kameda et al. (2021)](https://doi.org/10.1016/j.icarus.2021.114348). Units are µm⁻¹; it is neither terrain slope nor a mineral identification.

entries.subject: Hydration map from the NIRS3 2.72 µm band depth
entries.finding: No lens. No archive or paper releases a band-depth map: the JADE2 product list has only ONC and TIR maps, and Kitazato et al. (2019) released calibrated spectra only. Their mapped quantity (Fig. 2E-F) is the band intensity normalised by its trend with surface temperature, defined in supplementary material we could not read. Coverage is not the problem: the 105 proximity sequences of the Thermal Excess Removed bundle (urn:jaxa:darts:hyb2_nirs3_sp::1.0, L2d v04) hold 414,360 complete footprints, median 24 m across (5-95%: 3.6-51 m) on a 448 m-radius body, covering 99.7% of 1° cells with incidence and emission below 70°; the 19 July 2018 scan alone covers 96%. The band itself is uniform. With the Bott et al. (2022) definition (continuum through channels 80 and 85, 2.684 and 2.773 µm; depth at channel 82, 2.720 µm), the 19 July 2018 scan gives 7.1-10.0% (5-95%), matching the published 7-10%. Averaged in 10° cells, four global scans (11 and 19 July 2018, 1 May and 31 October 2019) vary by only 0.31-0.57 percentage points around 8.1-8.6%, while one cell mean carries 0.17-0.43 points of noise. The pattern does not repeat. Cell means from two scans correlate at 0.60 and 0.35-0.37 only when their estimated temperature maps agree (r = 0.98 and 0.75-0.79). With differing temperature maps, the correlation is 0.03-0.07. After removing each scan's temperature trend, it is 0.08-0.39. A colour map would mostly show thermal-removal and viewing-geometry residuals, not hydration differences. Kitazato et al. (2019) found no clear link between the normalised intensity and terrain, and Bott et al. (2022) found no statistically significant band-depth differences between spectral classes.
entries.revisitWhen: JAXA or the NIRS3 team releases a band-depth map, or the photometrically corrected L3A spectra that Wargnier et al. (2026) say will be archived show a band-depth pattern that repeats between independent scans.
